items.title: D-St set for a negative opening as GIFT Nifty signals weak start
items.description: Benchmark indices opened flat on Tuesday but gained momentum, closing in positive territory. This uptick was supported by easing Brent crude oil prices and a stronger rupee. Analysts predict continued consolidation within a range of 24,700 to 25,500 going forward.

items.title: Ribbit Capital sells Groww shares worth Rs 1,905 crore
items.description: The shares were bought by Societe Generale, Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, BlackRock, Fidelity Investments, BNP Paribas, Morgan Stanley Asia Singapore, HDFC Standard Life Insurance, NPS Trust, Norges Bank, among others.

items.title: Anand Rathi to gift shares worth Rs 30 cr to 5,000 employees and personal staff
items.description: The shares, representing about 0.08% of the company's equity capital, will be transferred from Rathi's personal holding, with each recipient eligible to receive up to 25 shares. Anand Rathi Wealth shares fell 0.5% to close at ₹2,273 on Tuesday. The transfer carries no monetary consideration linked to continued employment, and the company has obtained the necessary approval from Sebi, the release said.

items.title: Stocks in News: Tata Group companies, Bharti Airtel, HCL Tech, Groww, IIFL Finance, ACME Solar
items.description: Several stocks, including Tata Group companies, Bharti Airtel, HCLTech, Groww, IIFL Finance and ACME Solar Holdings, are likely to remain in focus on Wednesday, November 18, as investors track company-specific developments and corporate announcements.

items.title: Dalal Street’s top investors defy market slump; Mukul Agrawal tops Q2 wealth gains
items.description: For the study, only holdings in which these investors owned more than 1% equity in listed companies were considered.. Agrawal’s portfolio value rose 30% quarter-on-quarter (QoQ), the highest among the investors tracked, followed by Bhanshali and Kacholia, whose portfolios gained 15.5% and 12.5%, respectively.

items.title: Sensex, Nifty hit 9-month highs as bank stocks lead market rally
items.description: The BSE Sensex advanced 427.40 points, or 0.52%, to close at 82,532.19, while the NSE Nifty gained 96.30 points, or 0.38%, to settle at 25,387.40. Both benchmarks ended at their highest closing levels since February 2026, before the Iran-US conflict triggered a sharp selloff in global markets.

items.title: Stock Radar: Canara Bank stock showing signs of reversal; trades above crucial moving averages, says Gaurav Bissa
items.description: Canara Bank has recovered after hitting a significant support zone in October 2026. The stock has shown a steady upward trend over recent weeks, rising by more than 10%. Analysts suggest a target price of Rs 155 for traders in the coming weeks. The Relative Strength Index indicates positive momentum without being overbought currently. Traders are advised to place a stop loss below Rs 115 based on closing prices.

items.title: Payment firms seek clarity on MDR rollout for select UPI transactions
items.description: The Payments Council of India (PCI) has urged the finance ministry and NPCI to announce a firm timeline for implementing merchant discount rates (MDR) on select UPI transactions, after the proposed rollout was deferred until after Diwali.

items.title: Explained: Why did central banks just buy 320 tonnes of gold this quarter and can this last amid uncertainty?
items.description: Despite gold prices sliding to a one-year low, central banks are accelerating purchases. According to the World Gold Council, they bought 321 tonnes in Q3, up 8.5% from Q2 and sharply higher than Q1's 57 tonnes. Total purchases reached 675 tonnes in the first nine months of 2026, up 6% year-on-year.

items.title: Why is market falling today? Sensex slumps 700 points, Nifty below 25,200. 4 factors behind Rs 5 lakh crore wipeout
items.description: On Wednesday, the Indian stock market saw a notable decline, with Sensex and Nifty dropping significantly. A reduction of over Rs 5 lakh crore occurred in total market capitalization across listed stocks. The overall market breadth was negative, showcasing more declines than advances on the NSE. While several sectors faced losses, Nifty Pharma managed to maintain marginal gains. Notable stocks like Titan and Bajaj Finance contributed to the overall downturn.

items.title: How Ashish Kacholia, Radhakishan Damani, Madhusudan Kela and other ace investors reshuffled their portfolios in Q2
items.description: Some of India's most prominent individual investors in terms of their stock portfolio value, including Mukul Agrawal, Akash Bhanshali and Ashish Kacholia, emerged as the biggest portfolio gainers during the July-September quarter.However, the trend was not uniform across all ace investors. DMart founder Radhakishan Damani recorded the steepest decline in portfolio value among the prominent investors tracked, according to data from Prime Database.For the study, only holdings in which these investors owned more than 1% equity in listed companies were considered. Here are the top three stocks held by these individual investors and the stocks in which they increased or decreased their holdings.

items.title: Govt weighs tax tweaks to boost stock trading, curb derivatives: Report
items.description: The government is reviewing proposals to cut securities transaction tax on cash equities by 50% while raising levies on derivatives to curb speculative trading and encourage broader market participation. Officials are also considering a reduction in long-term capital gains tax. The recommendations will be presented to Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman ahead of Budget 2027.

items.title: SpiceJet shares rally 30% in 6 days even as flight cancellations leave passengers stranded at airports. What’s boosting the stock?
items.description: SpiceJet shares have rallied around 30% in six sessions, hitting the upper circuit for five consecutive days despite flight cancellations and operational disruptions. Expectations of a fresh capital raise and easing oil prices have boosted investor sentiment.

items.title: Sebi mulls linking MTF limits to free float; Angel One, BSE, Groww fall up to 7% from day’s high
items.description: In a recent announcement, SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey revealed that they are exploring the idea of connecting MTF limits to stock free float. This news has led to noticeable declines in shares of BSE, Angel One, NSE, and Groww, with Angel One experiencing a 7% dip from its day's peak and BSE shares dropping over 3%.

items.title: 16 microcap stocks surge up to 390% in CY26, emerge as multibaggers
items.description: While the benchmark Nifty 50 has slipped nearly 3% in CY26 so far, the Nifty Microcap 250 index has bucked the trend, delivering an impressive 13% gain. What's even more striking is that nearly 50 stocks in the microcap index have surged over 50%, with 16 emerging as multibaggers, more than doubling investors' wealth in just over 10 months of 2026.

items.title: PVR Inox shares jump 6% in 2 days, hit fresh 52-week high as CRISIL upgrades outlook to positive. What is it seeing
items.description: PVR Inox shares surged after CRISIL upgraded its outlook to 'Positive,' citing strong growth and enhanced operating margins as pivotal factors. The company's strategic diversification of content, coupled with a stable admissions landscape and expansion into southern India, fuels ongoing revenue increases. With a robust financial foundation, PVR Inox is well-positioned for sustained positive market performance.

items.title: 156% rally in one day! Why this drugmaker stock witnessed such skyrocketing jump on Wall Street
items.description: Sellas Life Sciences shares surged 156% after its experimental leukemia vaccine, galinpepimut-S (GPS), significantly extended survival in a late-stage trial. The treatment reduced death risk by 41%, with median survival reaching 24 months. The company plans FDA discussions, targeting an accelerated approval filing in 2027.

items.title: Max Healthcare among 10 Nifty stocks rallied up to 22% in 1 month. Did you miss the rally?
items.description: After being the world’s worst performing major equity market, Nifty is now suddenly the best one and has rallied around 10% so far in November as bluechip stocks have now become favourites of foreign institutional investors (FIIs) as they move out of crowded AI markets such as South Korea and Taiwan. The just-concluded Q2 earnings season, which saw Nifty recording 27% YoY profit growth also boosted sentiments. Here are the top 10 performing Nifty stocks in last one month:

items.title: ACME Solar shares rally 3% as subsidiary signs 150 MW hybrid power project PPA with NTPC
items.description: ACME Solar shares rose after its subsidiary signed a 150 MW hybrid power purchase agreement with NTPC at a tariff of Rs 3.21 per unit. The project combines solar, wind and energy storage, taking the company's under-construction, PPA-backed portfolio to 5,080 MW.

items.title: Bank stocks hit record highs, but is the rally just getting started? Analysts cite tailwinds for more upside ahead
items.description: Bank Nifty has surged nearly 25% from its April lows to hit a record high above 62,440. Easing oil prices, a revival in FII inflows, strong credit growth and attractive valuations have lifted sentiment. Analysts remain positive on select large-cap private banks and see further opportunities across the sector.

items.title: HFCL, Sterlite Tech shares rally 5% each as Nvidia’s strong earnings eclipse AI worries
items.description: HFCL and Sterlite Technologies shares rally 5% each as Nvidia's better-than-expected earnings and revenue outlook revive optimism around AI infrastructure spending. The gains follow a decline of more than 10% in both stocks over two sessions. Investors are also assessing concerns around US data centre expansion and AI sector valuations.

items.title: Ashoka Buildcon shares rise 9% after firm wins contract for NHAI project worth Rs 1465 crore
items.description: Ashoka Buildcon shares surged up to 9% after the company emerged as the lowest bidder for an Rs 1,465 crore NHAI project to complete an eight-lane stretch of the Vadodara-Mumbai Expressway in Gujarat. The EPC project has an 18-month completion deadline, adding to the company’s infrastructure order pipeline.

items.title: Global money rushes back into Indian stocks at record pace
items.description: Foreign investors have poured a record $9.61 billion into Indian equities so far in November, marking a sharp reversal after months of selling. Improving earnings prospects, easing crude prices and weakness in the global AI trade are driving renewed interest, with India emerging as one of Asia’s preferred equity markets.

items.title: India Inc’s earnings upgrades outnumber downgrades. What Jefferies sees ahead for investors
items.description: India’s earnings recovery is gaining momentum, with analyst upgrades outnumbering downgrades for a second straight quarter. Jefferies raised its FY27 earnings estimate for MSCI India, while stronger revenue growth across sectors offered signs of improving demand, despite persistent margin pressures.

items.title: These mid-caps have ‘strong buy’ and ‘buy’ recos and upside potential of over 25%, according to analysts
items.description: More than anything else, what is important in the stock market at this point of time is to avoid a hybrid model of thinking. What this basically means is: Don’t buy stocks for the short term and, if they fall, keep them for the long term.

items.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Thursday
items.description: Indian markets ended lower on November 18 as profit booking and global headwinds interrupted the recent rally. Sensex fell 500 points and Nifty lost 159 points, while broader indices declined. Analysts highlighted FPI inflows, banking stocks and earnings growth.

items.title: Market Trading Guide: Deepak Fertilisers among 3 stock recommendations for Thursday
items.description: Benchmark indices witnessed profit booking and closed in negative amid weak global cues, reversing some of the recent gains. However, easing Brent crude oil prices, which remained below the $95 mark, and appreciation in the rupee provided some support to investor sentiment, limiting the overall pressure. The Nifty 50 slipped 159 points, or 0.63%, to settle at 25,228, while the BSE Sensex declined 500 points, or 0.61%, to close at 82,032.Here are 3 stock recommendations for Thursday

items.title: Dalmia Bharat to consider share buyback at Nov 23 board meeting
items.description: Dalmia Bharat, India's fourth-largest cement manufacturer, will hold a board meeting on November 23. The meeting will focus on a proposal for a buyback of fully paid-up equity shares. Specific details regarding the buyback size, price, and number of shares have not been disclosed yet. The company also plans to expand its cement capacity to 75 million tonnes per annum by FY28.

items.title: Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, BNP Paribas buy IIFL Finance shares as Fairfax sells stake in Rs 3,500-crore block deals
items.description: Fairfax-backed FIH Mauritius sold 13.24% of IIFL Finance for Rs 3,488 crore through block deals, attracting global financial institutions and domestic mutual funds. The stake sale follows IIFL Finance's proposed Rs 6,414-crore capital raise involving Blackstone.

items.title: ANMI seeks removal of STT on delivery trades, LTCG exemption in Budget 2027-28
items.description: ANMI has urged the government to overhaul market taxation in Budget 2027-28, seeking STT removal on delivery trades, LTCG exemption, revised trading income classification, Section 88E rebate restoration and an extended loss carry-forward period.

items.title: PSBs' net profit rises 17% to Rs 1.10 lakh cr in H1 FY27; business crosses Rs 300 lakh crore
items.description: Public sector banks in India have reported a remarkable 16.9 percent rise in net profits during the first half of this fiscal year, reflecting a thriving financial environment. With total business reaching Rs 301.6 lakh crore, and a notable drop in the gross non-performing assets ratio to an unprecedented 1.69 percent, the banks are demonstrating improved stability.

items.title: Two Trades for Today: A top pharma company for a 5.5% rise, a mid-cap media stock for a gain of about 7%
items.description: Our technical analysts identify select stocks every trading day that may gain momentum even in volatile markets. Here are the technical calls for today.

items.title: Kotak MF, BlackRock, others buy stake worth Rs 1,905 cr in Groww
items.description: Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund (MF) led the buying spree, acquiring 2.05 crore shares or a 0.33 per cent stake, for Rs 448.95 crore, making it the biggest buyer in the transaction.

items.title: Market wrap:  SBI, Cipla, Titan Company, HDFC Life top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Wednesday
items.description: Indian equity benchmarks ended lower on Wednesday as profit booking dragged the Sensex down 500 points and the Nifty 159 points. Titan Company and HDFC Life led the losses, while SBI and Cipla topped the gainers. Analysts flagged 25,000 as a crucial support level for the Nifty.

items.title: PI Industries among 5 stocks hitting 52-week low; slipped up to 26% in a month
items.description: Benchmark Sensex fell 500 points to close at 82,032 on Wednesday. Amid the market decline, five stocks from the BSE 500 Index touched fresh 52-week lows, hitting their lowest price levels in the past year. A 52-week low refers to the lowest price at which a stock has traded over the past year and is commonly used as an indicator of its recent price performance.

items.title: Largecaps pull ahead of small and mid caps in Q2 profit growth by over 25%. What’s driving the gap?
items.description: Largecap companies have overtaken small and midcaps in profit growth in Q2 FY27, with the gap exceeding 25 percentage points. Nuvama attributes the shift to stronger margins and commodity exposure among largecaps, while manufacturing-focused smaller companies faced pressure. However, analysts expect the earnings growth gap to narrow ahead.

items.title: Time for less fear, more diligence? 5 small-cap stocks from different sectors with upside potential of up to 29%
items.description: It is no longer the time to be bearish on small-cap stocks simply out of habit. But it is very much the time to be selective, to do some homework on companies, and not to buy indiscriminately.

items.title: SpiceJet board approves up to Rs 5,500 crore fundraise amid operational challenges; stock hits 5% upper circuit
items.description: SpiceJet's board of directors announced a fundraising plan to raise up to Rs 5,500 crore. The airline's shares have surged significantly, hitting the upper circuit for six consecutive sessions. Flight cancellations and operational disruptions have caused significant challenges for SpiceJet in recent days. The airline is focusing on rebuilding capacity and ensuring operational reliability going forward. The fundraising aims to strengthen its financial position and support fleet expansion efforts.

items.title: Nifty target 28,500: Why Goldman Sachs is betting on India’s mean reversion
items.description: Goldman Sachs has upgraded Indian equities to overweight, citing resilient domestic demand, a broadening earnings recovery and historically low foreign investor positioning. It expects the Nifty to reach 28,500 by end-2027, implying 12% upside. The bank sees earnings growth accelerating to 15% in 2027 and 2028, and calls India a “clear AI diversification contender” for global investors.

items.title: Stock Radar: Kalyan Jewellers stock breaks out from inverted head & shoulder pattern to hit fresh 52-week high; time to buy?
items.description: Kalyan Jewellers Ltd has recently broken out from an inverted head and shoulder pattern in November 2026. Experts suggest short-term traders may buy the stock for a target above 800 levels soon. The stock found strong support above 300 levels before rebounding, indicating a potential bullish reversal. Current momentum indicators show a positive outlook with sustained strength in price structure.
